notes: Pages: Paphlagonia, Pharnaces I, Kingdom of Pontus, Mithridates VI and Aristonicus of Pergamon (the last three opened for sister dossiers). Cliopatria rows: the shape (22.9 k km2) ends -127; the Mithridates VI page puts the partition at the 108 BC invasion ('probably') and the Kingdom of Pontus page gives it no year, so the end is -108 and a keyframe (-126..-108) keeps the shape. Disagreement: the Paphlagonia page says Mithridates Ctistes controlled most of Paphlagonia from 302-266 and that after Sinope fell in 183 'the whole province was part of Pontus' (until 65), while the Pharnaces I page (179 peace), the Aristonicus page (Pylaemenes of Paphlagonia, 133-129) and the Kingdom of Pontus page (partition, undated) show a separate Paphlagonia; the dossier follows the latter three. Gaps: no page opened gives a founding date, a capital or a ruler list ('the rulers appear to have borne the name Pylaimenes', no dates); capitals is left empty. The Senate's 97 order that Nicomedes leave Paphlagonia and Pompey's leaving 'the interior to native princes' (65) suggest a native Paphlagonia after 108, which Cliopatria does not draw and the pages opened do not date; a gap-filler should open 'Pylaemenes' and 'Paphlagonia (Roman)' pages. The Kingdom of Pontus dossier carries the matching gain (108) and loss (63) events with counterpart paphlagonia. REVIEW REPAIR 2026-10-19: the end moved from -116 to -108 after the reviewer found that no page opened gave c. 116 (the Kingdom of Pontus page has no timeline; its only '116' is Ariarathes VI's murder); the dissolve, keyframe, war, certainty and successor texts follow. The Kingdom of Pontus dossier moved its matching gain to -108, as did the Galatia dossier's loss. Thin item tried: the 'Pylaemenes' page is about a mythological king of the Eneti and gives no capital, founding date or ruler list, so capitals stays empty and a native Paphlagonia after 108 (Senate order, Pompey) remains a gap.
